6º de Primaria · Inglés

Present simple and continuous

Ficha para imprimir
123456
1

Pregunta de arranquePiensa 30 segundos antes de seguir

«I play football» y «I'm playing football» se traducen casi igual: «juego al fútbol» y «estoy jugando al fútbol». ¿Cuándo usarías cada una?

Escribe o di en voz alta tu respuesta. Después .

«I play football» habla de algo que haces normalmente, por ejemplo todos los sábados. «I'm playing football» habla de algo que pasa ahora mismo, mientras lo dices. En inglés esta diferencia es muy importante.

2

Aprende9 bloques cortos

Two presents

English has two present tenses. The present simple is for things we do often or things that are always true: «I walk to school every day», «Water boils at 100 °C». The present continuous is for things that are happening now: «Look! It's raining».

En castellano: el presente simple sirve para rutinas y verdades; el presente continuo, para lo que está pasando en este momento. En español también tenemos las dos formas («leo» y «estoy leyendo»), pero en inglés hay que elegir con más cuidado.

Present simple: affirmative

To make the present simple, use the verb without to: «I play», «you play», «we play», «they play». With he, she and it add -s: «she plays», «it rains».

Spelling (ortografía): verbs ending in -sh, -ch, -ss, -x and -o add -es: watch → watches, go → goes, do → does. Consonant + y changes to -ies: study → studies, fly → flies. But vowel + y only adds -s: play → plays. Have is irregular: he has.

Present simple: negatives and questions

For negatives we use don't (do not) or doesn't (does not) + verb: «I don't like fish», «He doesn't like fish». Careful: after doesn't the verb has no -s.

For questions we put Do or Does first: «Do you like pizza?» – «Yes, I do. / No, I don't». «Does she speak French?» – «Yes, she does. / No, she doesn't». En castellano: en inglés la pregunta no se hace solo con la entonación, como en «¿te gusta la pizza?»; necesita el ayudante do/does.

Time words for the present simple

Some words tell us to use the present simple. They are frequency adverbs (adverbios de frecuencia): always, usually, often, sometimes, never. They go before the main verb but after the verb to be: «I usually have cereal», «She is always happy».

Other time expressions go at the end: every day, every Monday, on Saturdays, at the weekend, once a week. Example: «We go swimming twice a week». En castellano: «twice a week» es «dos veces por semana».

Present continuous: form

The present continuous has two parts: the verb to be (am / is / are) and the verb with -ing. «I am reading», «She is eating», «They are playing». In speaking we use short forms: I'm, she's, they're.

Spelling: verbs ending in -e lose the e: write → writing, dance → dancing. Short verbs ending in consonant + vowel + consonant double the last letter: swim → swimming, run → running, sit → sitting. Negative: «I'm not sleeping». Question: «Are you listening?» – «Yes, I am».

Vídeo: Present Continuous Verb Chant: What are you doing? · ELF Kids Videos (YouTube) · 2,8 millones de visualizaciones

Time words for the present continuous

These words tell us that something is happening now: now, right now, at the moment, today, this week, and also Look! and Listen! «Look! The baby is walking!», «Be quiet! Grandpa is sleeping».

We also use the present continuous for temporary things (cosas temporales): «I usually live in Madrid, but this month I'm staying with my aunt in Cádiz». En castellano: si algo pasa solo durante un tiempo, aunque no sea en este segundo exacto, también va en continuo.

Simple or continuous?

Compare: «My dad works in a hospital» (that is his job, always) and «My dad is working in the garden» (now, at this moment). «Sara speaks English» (she can, always) and «Sara is speaking English» (now, on the phone).

Some verbs are almost never in continuous: like, love, hate, want, know, understand, need. We say «I know the answer», not «I'm knowing». En castellano: son verbos de gustos, deseos y pensamientos; no son acciones que se ven, por eso van en simple.

Reading: a day at summer camp

Read Marta's message: «Hi Grandma! I'm at summer camp. Every day I get up at eight and I have breakfast with my friends. We usually go canoeing in the morning. I don't like the food very much, but the activities are fantastic! Right now I'm sitting by the lake and my friends are playing volleyball. The sun is shining. Love, Marta».

Find the two presents: the routine (get up, have, go, don't like) and the things happening now (am sitting, are playing, is shining).

Let's practise: picture game

Play in pairs. One student mimes an action (hace mímica) and the other asks: «Are you swimming?» – «No, I'm not». «Are you dancing?» – «Yes, I am!». Then change roles.

Second round: talk about your routine. «Do you walk to school?», «What time do you go to bed?», «How often do you play video games?». Answer with full sentences: «I sometimes play at the weekend». Consejo: escucha si la pregunta empieza por Are (ahora) o por Do (normalmente).

Ejemplos resueltos

Ejemplo 1. Complete with the present simple: «My brother (watch) ___ TV every evening.»

  1. My brother = he → hay que añadir -s.
  2. watch acaba en -ch → -es.

Resultado: My brother watches TV every evening.

Ejemplo 2. Complete with the present continuous: «Listen! The birds (sing) ___.»

  1. Listen! indica que pasa ahora → presente continuo.
  2. The birds = they → are.
  3. sing + -ing = singing.

Resultado: Listen! The birds are singing.

Ejemplo 3. Choose: «I (understand / am understanding) the question.»

  1. understand es un verbo de pensamiento.
  2. Estos verbos casi nunca van en continuo.

Resultado: I understand the question.

Errores típicos

  • Olvidar la -s con he/she/it: «she play» → «she plays».
  • Poner -s después de doesn't: «he doesn't likes» → «he doesn't like».
  • Olvidar el verbo to be en el continuo: «I reading» → «I'm reading».
  • No doblar la consonante: «swiming», «runing» → «swimming», «running».
  • Usar el continuo con like, want o know: «I'm wanting» → «I want».

Ejercicios

Hazlos en tu cuaderno y después abre la solución.

  1. Write the he/she form: go, fly, wash, have.

    Ver solución
    goes, flies, washes, has.

  2. Write the -ing form: write, swim, play, sit.

    Ver solución
    writing, swimming, playing, sitting.

  3. Make it negative: «Tom likes carrots.»

    Ver solución
    Tom doesn't like carrots.

  4. Make a question: «They live in Seville.»

    Ver solución
    Do they live in Seville?

  5. Complete: «Look! The cat (climb) ___ the tree.»

    Ver solución
    is climbing.

  6. Complete: «We (have) ___ English on Mondays.»

    Ver solución
    have.

  7. Put the adverb in the right place: «I am late. (never)»

    Ver solución
    I am never late.

  8. Correct the mistake: «She is knowing the answer.»

    Ver solución
    She knows the answer.

  9. Translate: «Normalmente voy en bici, pero hoy estoy caminando.»

    Ver solución
    I usually go by bike, but today I'm walking.

  10. Write two sentences about you: one routine and one thing you are doing now.

    Ver solución
    Model answer: I play basketball on Tuesdays. Now I'm doing my English homework.

Para familias

  • Durante la cena, preguntad en inglés «What are you doing?» y «What do you do on Saturdays?» y comparad las respuestas.
  • Narrad en voz alta lo que hace alguien en un vídeo sin sonido: «He's running, he's jumping…».
  • Repasad juntos las tarjetas del paso 6 dos minutos al día durante una semana.

Para profesores

Saberes: Comunicación oral y escrita sobre rutinas, hábitos y acciones en curso; presente simple y continuo (Lengua Extranjera) (RD 157/2022, tercer ciclo de Primaria).

  • Mímica por parejas con preguntas Are you…?
  • Encuesta de rutinas de la clase con How often do you…? y gráfico de resultados.
  • Describir una foto del patio en presente continuo.

Qué vas a aprender

  • Use the present simple for habits and facts (hábitos y verdades)
  • Use the present continuous for actions happening now (ahora mismo)
  • Make negatives and questions with do/does and am/is/are
  • Choose the right tense with time words: every day, now, at the moment
